_comment: Every entry needs a reason. These are strings the product must be able to say because they are functional, not promotional: either the user is downloading a component from where its publisher puts it, or they are configuring a notification channel. An entry is matched either as an exact i18n key or as a substring of the offending literal.
bug.channel_github_desc: Label for the bug-report channel in the Help menu. It tells the user the report is public and pre-filled, which is a warning about where their data goes, not an advertisement.
app.report_bug_not_configured: Toast shown when the bug tracker is not configured for this install. Naming the missing setting is the only way the message is actionable.
issues/new?title=: The bug-report URL built in Header.tsx. BugReportMenuLinks.test.tsx asserts it targets this product's own repository, and the same file already asserts that no upstream contact surface remains. Three test files guard a fixed defect here (the menu used to open the tracker with an empty body) and the rule that the report is written in English whatever language the UI is in. Filing a bug is a support function, not a promotional link.
integrations.telegram: Telegram as a notification channel the workspace configures for its own alerts, alongside Slack and Teams. It is an integration, not a community link.
integrations.intro_: Same as integrations.telegram: the notification-channel setup copy.
boq.source_open: The button opens the item's source document in its viewer. 'Open source' here is the verb 'open' plus the noun 'source document', not the licence term. The key is allowlisted rather than the phrase, so no real use of the phrase is exempted.
openconstructionerp-server: The name of the Windows background service the desktop app installs. An internal identifier the user has to be able to read to find the service in services.msc; the constraints require keeping internal identifiers.
pip install openconstructionerp: The package name in an install command the user is told to run. Internal identifier, not promotion.
github.com/datadrivenconstruction/cad2da: Where the publisher puts the DWG/DXF converter this product downloads and runs. A truthful functional dependency: without the URL the converter cannot be fetched, and the constraints require keeping upstream-published artefacts.
github.com/datadrivenconstruction/OpenCo: Where the publisher puts CWICR, the cost-database engine. Same reason as the converter URL.
by Data Driven Construction: Provenance of the CWICR cost dataset the user is importing. Naming the dataset's author is a truthful statement about data they are about to rely on, not a claim about this product.
BGE-M3: Names the third-party embedding model the search client needs, and where it comes from. Describing a dependency's licence is factual; it says nothing about this product being open source.
settings.converter_view_source: Opens the installed converter's own source location so an operator can verify what is running on their machine. Functional provenance for a binary the product executes.
bim.auto_install_failed_body: The DWG/DXF/RVT/IFC converter this product runs is not bundled: its publisher distributes the binary through their own release feed, and the installer, the up-to-date check and the manual fallback all have to tell the user where that feed is or the feature cannot work. The constraints require keeping the dependency on upstream-published artefacts. What is stated is where a required component comes from, never that this product is open source.

costs.load_failed_unreachable: The cost/price databases are downloaded from a data host, and these are the messages shown when that host cannot be reached or when a phase of the download is running. Naming the host is what makes the failure actionable - 'could not reach the data host' with no host leaves an operator with nothing to allow through a firewall. Same functional-provenance reason as the converter.

demo_read_only.install_python: The internal package identifier, in the one place a user has to type it. The constraints require keeping internal identifiers, and an install command that does not name the package cannot be run.
match_readiness.search_client_missing: The internal package identifier, in the one place a user has to type it. The constraints require keeping internal identifiers, and an install command that does not name the package cannot be run.
dataSecurity.source_link: The Data Security panel lists where each dataset the product can load comes from, and this is the link to that source. Knowing the provenance of data you are about to price construction work with is the point of the panel, and it is the same truthful-dependency class as the CWICR dataset provenance the Part D constraints require keeping. It says where a dataset comes from, not that this product is open source.
